sections.title: Giant sequoia
sections.text: This plate represents Sequoiadendron giganteum, the giant sequoia, an evergreen conifer native to groves on the western slopes of California’s Sierra Nevada. Mature trees commonly reach about 76 m tall and 3–6 m in trunk diameter above the basal swell; the tallest recorded is 94.5 m. It is the largest tree by trunk volume, while the related coast redwood grows taller.

sections.title: Bark, cones and life cycle
sections.text: The massive, fluted trunk has reddish fibrous bark. The short, awl-like leaves clasp the shoots, and the ovoid cones are about 4–7 cm long. The species is long-lived and fire-adapted; no food use is established in the cited sources.
